newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends at session low, but holds support.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends at session low, but holds support.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures failed to recover from last week's heavy losses on Monday, and fell rapidly in late trade to close at the session low.
July Brent closed 16 cents down at $17.54 a barrel -- the yearly spot low on the continuation chart -- having shed 62 cents in Friday's session.
"We had a couple of pushes to the upside but this market just isn't ready for it," said one broker.
Earlier, June gas oil ended the day $4.25 a tonne down at $160.00, having caught up with Brent's late losses on Friday.
"(The market is) still reeling from the shock of all the fund liquidation throughout last week," said one broker.
But traders said that Brent's holding of support at $17.54 was a positive sign.
"We were headed down to $17.50, we didn't quite make it, so we might go up from here," said one.
Investment funds baled out of the oil market en masse on Friday, unimpressed by U.S. gasoline demand with the driving season now supposedly well underway.
July NYMEX crude broke key support and hit a 15 month low. The contract slid a further 14 cents to $18.65 on Monday.
"Crude just doesn't seem to be able to recover from its technical failure," said one broker in New York.
NYMEX unleaded gasoline futures made modest gains on the open, but quickly slid into negative territory to close at the session low of 56.10 cents a gallon.
Weekly U.S. stocks data from the American Petroleum Institute (API) to be released after the close of trade on Tuesday will give a fresh indication of gasoline consumption.
"We're waiting for the APIs now, but I don't think we're expecting anything to turn this market around," said one broker.
Last week's renewal of the United Nations oil-for-food deal with Iraq for a further six-months was still providing a bearish backdrop to the market, dealers said.
The market was unmoved by reports that many European buyers don't expect to lift their first barrels until July.
